265: Shinsatsu  are a type of thaumaturgic talisman (also known as  gofu ) distributed at shrines and symbolic of a spiritual being or its supranormal power.  Shinsatsu  may be made of wood, paper, or metal and bear a written or printed inscription. The term is generally used to refer to the relatively large kind of amulets enshrined in   kamidana  , or affixed above gates, on doors and pillars, or on ceilings. Their origins lie in the talismans made by priests of  onmyōdō  (Chinese yin-yang divination) or at Buddhist temples, which later came to be produced at shrines as well.
